texts.p_bossy-r: Two new ideas today, and both are about bossy r. First: when R comes after the letter A, or the letter O, it changes the sound. A, R says [[ɑɹ|ar]], like star. O, R says [[ɔɹ|or]], like corn. Second: E, R, and I, R, and U, R all say the same sound, [[ɝ|er]], like her, bird, and fur. You have to remember which one each word uses.
texts.p_ck-sh: Two new ideas today. First: at the end of a short word, after a short vowel, the k sound is spelled c, k, like sock and duck. Second: some letters team up to make one new sound. S, H says [[ʃ|sh]], like fish. C, H says [[tʃ|ch]], like chin. And T, H says [[θ|th]], like bath.
texts.p_double: Two new ideas today. First: at the end of a short word, right after a short vowel, f, l, s, and z are doubled, like puff, shell, dress, and buzz. Second: heart words. Most of a heart word follows the rules, but one part is tricky, so we learn that part by heart, like the a, i in said.
texts.p_endings: Two new ideas today, both about adding the endings i, n, g and e, d. First: double it. When a short word ends with one short vowel and one consonant, double that last letter before the ending. Hop becomes hopping, and clap becomes clapped. Second: drop the e. When a word ends in a silent e, drop the e before i, n, g. Bake becomes baking. For e, d, just add the d: smile becomes smiled.
texts.p_ng-tch: Two new ideas today. First: glued sounds. N and g glue together, like ring and song. N and k glue together, like pink and trunk. Second: right after a short vowel, the [[tʃ|ch]] sound is spelled t, c, h, like match. And the [[dʒ|j]] sound is spelled d, g, e, like badge.
texts.p_oi-ou: Two new ideas today. First: O, I and O, Y both say [[ɔɪ|oy]], like coin and toy. O, I goes in the middle of a word, and O, Y goes at the end. Second: O, U and O, W both say [[aʊ|ow]], like cloud and crown. O, U goes in the middle. O, W goes at the end, or before n or l, like cow, town, and owl.
texts.p_prefix: Two new ideas today, and both are prefixes: letters added to the front of a word to change what it means. First: U, N means not, like unhappy, and R, E means again, like redo. Second: D, I, S means the opposite, like dislike, and P, R, E means before, like preheat. Spell the prefix first, then the word you already know.
texts.p_review-1: Review time! This wing mixes everything from levels one, two, and three: c, k at the end, the letter teams s, h, and c, h, and t, h, bossy r, double letters, and heart words. Show what you know!
texts.p_review-2: Review time! This wing mixes everything from levels five, six, and seven: silent e, soft c and soft g, the glued sounds n, g and n, k, the endings t, c, h and d, g, e, and the vowel teams. Show what you know!
texts.p_review-3: Review time! This wing mixes everything from levels nine, ten, and eleven: prefixes like un, [[ɹi|re]], dis, and pre, the [[ɔɪ|oy]] and [[aʊ|ow]] sounds, and the endings i, n, g and e, d. Show what you know!
texts.p_review-4: Review time! This is the grand finale wing. It mixes everything from levels thirteen, fourteen, and fifteen: changing y to i, adding s or e, s, suffixes like ful and less, and words with two syllables. Show what you know!
texts.p_silent-e: Two new ideas today. First: silent e. An e at the end of a word is silent, but it makes the vowel say its name. Kit becomes kite. Second: soft c and soft g. When c comes before e, i, or y, it says [[s|s]], like city. When g comes before e, i, or y, it often says [[dʒ|j]], like gem.
texts.p_suffix: Two new ideas today, and both are suffixes: endings that change a word. First: F, U, L means full of, like helpful, and L, E, S, S means without, like careless. Remember, the ending F, U, L has only one l. Second: L, Y tells how something is done, like slowly, and N, E, S, S turns a word into a thing, like kindness.
texts.p_syllables: Two new ideas today, both about longer words. First: two syllables. Clap the word into two parts and spell each part, like rab, bit, rabbit, and pic, nic, picnic. Second: consonant plus l, e. Many words end with a consonant and l, e, like table, apple, and purple. The e is silent.
texts.p_teams: Two new ideas today, and both are vowel teams: two letters that make one long sound. First: long a and long e. A, I goes in the middle, like rain, and A, Y goes at the end, like play. Long e is E, E or E, A, like tree and leaf. Second: long o and long i. O, A goes in the middle, like boat, and O, W goes at the end, like snow. Long i can be I, G, H, like light, or I, E, like pie.
texts.p_ytoi: Two new ideas today. First: y to i. When a word ends with a consonant and a y, change the y to i before you add an ending. Cry becomes cried, and happy becomes happier. Second: s or e, s. Most words just add s, like hats. Words that end in s, x, z, c, h, or s, h add e, s, like boxes and dresses. And when you add e, s to a y word, change the y to i too, like babies.
